title: Aiken Avenue Area Linkage Study
short_description: Connectivity study to improve pedestrian and area links in the City of Rensselaer.
project_location: City of Rensselaer, Albany County, New York, USA
project_scope: Linkage and transportation study for the Aiken Avenue, Ring Street, and 2nd Avenue area and the Columbia Street and Broadway area, focused on improving overall connectivity, including pedestrian connectivity. No specific structural works, spans, or building areas are stated.
services: Request for expressions of interest for civil engineering, planning/master planning, traffic design engineering, and transportation planning services; study duration 12 months.
relevance_explanation:
- This is a linkage/transportation study, not a bridge, building, roof, stadium, or special structure project.
- Scope is primarily planning, master planning, and traffic/transportation planning.
- No structural design task, no defined engineering structure, and no planning phases for a complex load-bearing structure are indicated.
- The sbp guidance explicitly rejects pure urban/open space planning, landscape, urban design, and feasibility-style studies.
- Very low construction budget further indicates limited structural relevance.
construction_cost_explanation: Taken from the tender documents: Total Construction Cost $60.0K.
fee_explanation: No explicit fee information is provided. The notice only states a 12-month study with planning and transportation disciplines requested.
references_qualifications: Qualified firms or individuals are sought; specific minimum references or qualification thresholds are not stated in the provided text.
contracting_authority: Capital District Transportation Committee, Albany, New York, USA. Contact: Carrie Ward. Phone: 518-458-2161. Fax: 518-459-2155. Email: info@capitalmpo.org. Website: https://www.nyscr.ny.gov/Ads/Details/2137163
notes: Although pedestrian connectivity is mentioned, the notice describes a linkage study rather than a bridge project. Category assigned by closest fit, but the project is essentially a transportation/planning study and not structurally relevant for sbp.
